reading: Grey (5) pieces at the bottom are lifted into the matching holes of the red (2) band at the top, each piece fitting exactly into a hole, and recoloured blue (1); the bottom area is cleared.

slots.pieces: grey objects in the lower area
slots.holes: background cavities open downward in the red band
slots.placement: each piece translated (upward, possibly sideways) so it exactly fills one hole
slots.colour: placed pieces become 1; original piece cells cleared

why: every hole in the red band is filled exactly by one grey piece of the same shape; no piece overlaps red

reading: The output is the red square outline cut from the input, with the small 3x3 coloured shape scaled up by an integer factor to exactly fill the outline's interior.

slots.container: the red rectangular outline (output = its box)

why: output size equals the outline's box; interior equals the shape's 3x3 box upscaled by interior/3

reading: Every hollow 3x3 square (8 cells around a background hole) is replaced by a red (2) plus of the same box; other shapes stay.

new_rows.name: ring_centre
new_rows.datalog:
fgc(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
nb(Y, X, count(DY, DX)) :- px(Y, X, C), !fgc(Y, X), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, fgc(Y2, X2).
ring_centre(Y, X) :- nb(Y, X, N), N = 8.

why: at each background cell whose 8 neighbours are all foreground, the 3x3 box centred there becomes the plus 020/222/020 (corners cleared to 0); no other cell changes

reading: Objects of 4 or more cells fall straight down until they touch the bottom border; objects of 1-3 cells stay where they are.

new_rows.name: big_obj
new_rows.datalog:
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
big(O) :- osize(O, N), N > 3.
big_obj(Y, X) :- big(O), obj(O, Y, X).

why: each subject object keeps its shape and column and its lowest row becomes the last grid row (direction down every pair)

reading: Each 3x3 window that is entirely colour 0 is filled with blue (1); when two such windows overlap only the first in reading order is filled.

new_rows.name: zero_sq
new_rows.datalog:
z(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0).
zn(Y, X, count(DY, DX)) :- z(Y, X), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, z(Y2, X2).
ctr(Y, X) :- zn(Y, X, N), N = 8.
blocked(Y, X) :- ctr(Y, X), ctr(Y2, X2), Y2 < Y, D = Y - Y2, D <= 2, E = X - X2, E <= 2, F = X2 - X, F <= 2.
blocked(Y, X) :- ctr(Y, X), ctr(Y, X2), X2 < X, E = X - X2, E <= 2.
keep(Y, X) :- ctr(Y, X), !blocked(Y, X).
zero_sq(Y, X) :- keep(Y, X).
zero_sq(Y, X) :- keep(Yc, Xc), off(DY, DX), Y = Yc + DY, X = Xc + DX.

why: the 9 cells of each kept all-0 3x3 window become 1; nothing else changes (colour 0 is not always the background, so the row uses px(...,0))
invariants: all cells outside the filled windows

reading: The grid is 3x3 panels split by grey (5) lines; the panel containing a yellow 4 is copied into the panel whose position matches the 4's position inside its own panel, and all other panels are cleared.
verb: copy marked panel to indexed slot

slots.panels: nine 3x3 panels cut by grey separators
slots.index: the (row, col) of the 4 inside the source panel
slots.target: the panel at that (row, col) in the 3x3 panel layout

why: output panel at the 4's local position equals the source panel; every other panel is all 0; separators unchanged

reading: Under the large umbrella-shaped object, every column that holds a single marker below the umbrella is filled with the marker colour from just under the umbrella down to the bottom border; other markers stay.

new_rows.name: under_umbrella
new_rows.datalog:
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
maxs(max(N)) :- osize(O, N).
top(O) :- osize(O, N), maxs(N).
under_umbrella(Y, X) :- obj(M, Y, X), osize(M, N), N = 1, top(T), obj(T, Y2, X), Y2 < Y.

why: each source marker's column is coloured vertically from the first cell below the umbrella (obstacle, upward) to the bottom border (downward)

reading: Count the distinct colours of the 3x3 input: 1 colour gives a grey (5) top row, 2 colours give a grey main diagonal, 3 colours give a grey anti-diagonal; the rest is 0.

slots.count: number of distinct colours in the input
slots.pattern: 1 -> top row, 2 -> main diagonal, 3 -> anti-diagonal, drawn in 5 on 0

why: output is fully determined by the input's distinct-colour count

reading: Each L-tromino (2x2 box missing one cell) shoots a diagonal ray of its colour from its missing corner outward (away from the elbow) to the grid border; the missing corner cell itself stays empty.

slots.direction: diagonal from the elbow cell through the missing corner
slots.start: the cell just beyond the missing corner

why: each ray is a diagonal line of the object's colour from beyond the gap to the border

reading: The output places beside the input a left-right mirror of it with colours swapped (0 -> 8, 2 -> 0), on the side where the red shape touches the input's edge.

slots.side: right if the shape touches the right edge, left if it touches the left edge
slots.original: input kept unchanged on the other side

why: output width is twice the input; one half is the input, the other is its inverted mirror joined at the edge the shape touches
